entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Honourable Sri Justice J.Sreenivas Rao
 Writ Petition No.1780 Of 2023
Order:

The grievance of the petitioner is that the respondents are not paying the compensation in respect of the subject land i.e, Ac.28.37 gts. in Sy.Nos.155/38 and 155/39 situated at Mucherla Village of Kandakur Mandal, Ranga Reddy District.

2. Heard Sri K. Sravan Kumar Reddy, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner and Sri Ch. Ravi Kumar, learned Assistant Government Pleader attached to the office of the learned Advocate General appearing for respondent Nos.1 to 5.
3.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is the owner and possessor of the subject land and the respondents authorities have acquired his land along with other lands for the purpose of 'Hyderabad Pharmacity' and passed awards dated 01.04.2022 and 29.11.2022.

However,
the respondents have not paid compensation to the petitioner.

The action of the respondents is contrary to the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (Act No.30 of 2013) (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act')
and also violative of Article 300-A of the Constitution of India.
4. Learned Assistant Government Pleader submitted that there are rival claims in respect of the subject property.

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (Act No.30 of 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The petitioner as well as other persons is claiming rights and compensation over the subject property and the said dispute has to be decided by the competent authority as required under Section 76 of the Act.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner has not disputed the same.

6. Taking into consideration the above said submissions as well as the averments made in para 8 of the counter affidavit filed by respondent No.4, it reveals that the subject land is in dispute between the pattadars and possessors and the said dispute has to be decided by the competent authority as required under the provisions of Section 76 of the Act.

7. For the foregoing reasons, this Court without expressing any opinion on merits of the case,
respondent No.2 is directed to refer the dispute to the competent authority as required under Section 76 of the Act within a period of six (6) weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order and thereupon, the competent authority is directed to decide the said dispute between the parties as early as possible, preferably within a period of three (3) months from thereafter.
8. With the above directions, the writ petition is disposed of.
